texts.facts: Extensive arguments have been addressed on this application - unlike the scope of the provision which primarily is because of the fact that the dispute is between neighbours. Subsequent to the matter being posted for orders another application u/s 151 CPC was preferred, however, I am not disposing of the same and the same shall be dealt subsequently. He has sued for permanent and mandatory injunction arraying NDMC, TPDDL and Delhi Jal Board as defendant No. 2, 3 and 4. His immediate neighbour is arrayed as defendant No. 1. His grievance is that earlier the neighbours around the plaintiff's house used to keep Gate Keepers/'Chowkidars' at the entry point of the Block. In this manner the area was secured. However, the said system is defunct since the last four years and the plaintiff had been maintaining Gate Keepers and 'Chowkidars' from his own funds for 24 hours a day and also providing a 'Chowkidar' Booth and Electricity, Fan etc. Defendant No. 1 is the immediate neighbour and the 'Chowkidar' Booth/Porta Cabin was in existence near the wall of his house for the last more than 15 years, however, the same was being maintained by the plaintiff since the last four years. The respective 'chowkidars'/gate keepers booth/porta cabin on account of constant use, was in bad shape, therefore, the plaintiff from his own funds arranged for the wood etc. and commenced the process of refurbishing the same. It was observed that some portion of the street was not visible from the place where the Porta Cabin was being kept because of its low height and therefore, it was decided by the plaintiff to increase the height of the Porta Cabin so that the person/chowkidar sitting in the same could have a better view of the street and cars parked therein while sitting inside the Porta cabin. In this regard the repair work was going on and had to continue on the next day on 20.12.2013. On the said date at about 10.15 - 10.30 p.m. plaintiff was informed that local police had come in as much as defendant No. 1 had made a complaint in this reference. Plaintiff was taken to police station Model Town and from there to the hospital for conducting his medical tests at Jahangir Puri to some Vide This Order I Shall Dispose Of An ... vs Sh. Vipin Gandhi & Ors on 28 April, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183053694/ 1 hospital and he was again taken back to police station Model Town and directed that he should ensure that the Porta cabin be placed six feet away from the house of the defendant No. 1. To avoid any controversy the plaintiff had agreed to shift the same. Now the plaintiff explains that the reason for such an act or the impelling reason was that the defendant No. 1 was using his house for commercial purposes and was operating a coaching institute from the said house/residence apart from a commercial kitchen where he redresses stale eatables, collected from various places and supplies the same in the adjoining market of Model town -II. A better porta cabin would have exposed him. Elaborating further he stated that earlier defendant No. 1 was operating a commercial coaching institute M/s Economic Education from his residence, which was closed officially about ten years back, by an operation conducted by the officials of defendant No. 2. The defendant No. 1 had removed the hoarding/signboard of the same but is still continuing the same. Further the defendant No. 1 was not having any separate electricity connection commercial one for running such an establishment. The plaintiff further claims that that defendant No. 1 was also not reporting such earnings to the tax authorities. In these circumstance, it is the duty of the plaintiff to file the instant suit to inform defendant No. 2 to 4 about all such activities which are not permissible and which also causes loss to the exchequer. The following reliefs have been sought for:- a.Issue a decree of mandatory injunction, in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants, thereby directing the defendant No. 1, not to conduct/operate any commercial kitchen or commercial coaching centre from premises No. EA-7, Model Town-I, Delhi by using domestic water and electricity connection and without any license, from North Delhi Municipal Corporation as well as from other concerned authorities including Central Service Tax Authorities and the defendant No. 2 to 4 be directed to seal, the premises No. EA-7, Model Town-I, which is being used for running such commercial activities, wherein an unauthorised coaching centre and unauthorized commercial kitchen is being operated by using facilities made available in the premises for domestic use only. b. Issue a decree of permanent injunction, in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants, thereby perpetually injuncting them, from operating any commercial kitchen or commercial coaching centre from premises No. EA-7, Model Town-I, Delhi by using domestic water and electricity connection and without any license, from North Delhi Municipal Corporation as well as from other concerned authorities including Central Service Tax Authorities and the defendant No. 2 to 4 be directed to seal, the premises No. EA-7, Model Town-1, which is being used for running such commercial activities, wherein an unauthorized coaching centre and unauthorized commercial kitchen is being operated by using facilities made available in the premises for domestic use only. 4. The written statement was filed by defendant No. 1. Defendant No. 1 in preliminary objection contended that the suit was filed solely to harass the defendant No. 1. It was not filed with clean hands and the plaintiff had concealed various facts and if viewed holistically the plaint does not disclose any cause of action against the defendant. Further Vide This Order I Shall Dispose Of An ... vs Sh. Vipin Gandhi & Ors on 28 April, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183053694/ 2 plaintiff had no locus standi to file the suit in as much as the alleged commercial activities does not in any manner affect him. The plaintiff had also not complied with the provisions of section 80 of the CPC, 1908. No irreparable injury was caused upon the plaintiff. No balance of convenience lies in his suit. The suit is only a nefarious design to cause damage or to involve the defendant No.1 in a frivolous litigation. The defendant No. 1 had in fact allowed the plaintiff to park his car next to the boundary wall. The plaintiff was getting a booth installed at the corner of defendant No. 1 and upon being confronted he had abused the defendant and thereafter, only the police was called. His medical examination revealed that the plaintiff was drunk and later on before SHO P.S. Model Town plaintiff had assured that he would not get the chowkidar/gate keeper's booth installed outside 6 feet of the periphery of defendant No.1's house. This suit was only a counter blast to the complaint filed by the answering defendant. Right of privacy of the defendant was breached by installing a CCTV camera on the wall of the house of the plaintiff. On merits it was denied that there was any practice of keeping the the 'chowkidars' /gate keepers or that the said system is defunct for the last four years. The version of the plaintiff that the 'chowkidar' booth was in existence since the last 15 years was stated to be per se a false one for the reason that the plaintiff has himself claimed that he was living in the property since the year 2005. It was strongly denied that defendant was operating any commercial kitchen from his house. It was further denied that the defendant No. 1 was having any coaching institute. It was denied that the defendant was misusing the electricity connection or water connection without intimating the authorities. No cause of action arose. Dismissal of the suit was sought for. 5. Defendant No. 2/NDMC had also filed a separate written statement contending that the suit was barred by the provisions of section 477 and 478 of the DMC Act. The suit was also liable to be dismissed u/o 7 rule 11 CPC. In so far as the applicant running commercial kitchen or coaching centre , the area was inspected and such averments were found to be incorrect. 6. On behalf of the Delhi Jal Board also written statement was filed. It was contended that the suit was without any cause of action and plaintiff had wrongly impleaded the defendants. An inspection was conducted of the suit property wherein it was reflected that water connection was 25 years old and there was no commercial activities visible. 7. On behalf of defendant No. 3 also, separate written statement was filed. Broadly the version is that no complaint was made by the plaintiff to them regarding misuse or theft of electricity. Furthermore, the suit property was inspected by the TPDDL on 11.12.2013 and five electricity connections were found installed. It was evident that no commercial activity i.e. coaching classes or kitchen was running from the suit property.
texts.arguments: The pleas of the other defendants were also relied upon to contend that there is no merit in the suit. 9. Reply to this application was filed. It was contended that defendant No. 1 was indeed running institute by the name of M/s Economic Education Consultant and such details are available in google map and some other social sites. Plaintiff reiterated the version that commercial activity i.e. commercial kitchen is running from the suit premises as the same requires licence from the Food Department and adherence to the required safety standard. Delhi Municipal Corporation prescribes a usage for any building and commercial activity is not permissible. Dismissal of the application was sought for.

Plaintiff reiterated the version that commercial activity i.e. commercial kitchen is running from the suit premises as the same requires licence from the Food Department and adherence to the required safety standard. Delhi Municipal Corporation prescribes a usage for any building and commercial activity is not permissible. Dismissal of the application was sought for.
